What it means for testing: Needs reduced-gravity methods, not a field site
Sources: NASA Moon fact sheet (https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/moonfact.html); NASA Mars fact sheet (https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/marsfact.html)

Can Earth match it?: No: about 135 °C short of the Moon, 55 °C short of Mars's poles
What it means for testing: Cold-trap and ice-mining tests need cryogenic chambers
Sources: Scambos et al. 2018 (https://repository.library.noaa.gov/view/noaa/26979/noaa_26979_DS1.pdf); Sefton-Nash et al. 2013 (https://meetingorganizer.copernicus.org/EPSC2013/EPSC2013-864.pdf); NASA Mars in depth (https://solarsystem.nasa.gov/planets/mars/in-depth.amp)

Condition: Temperature in long-lit lunar polar spots
What it means for testing: Cold field tests are realistic for sunlit lunar polar operations
Sources: Air & Space (https://www.airspacemag.com/daily-planet/new-light-on-the-lunar-poles-156800678/); WEF on Scambos study (https://weforum.org/agenda/2018/06/scientists-record-earths-lowest-temperature-ever-heres-how-cold-it-got)

Can Earth match it?: Yes for Mars; more than 19 °C short of the Moon's day side
What it means for testing: Heat tests in the Lut exceed Mars's highs but fall short of the Moon's day side
Sources: Air & Space (https://www.airspacemag.com/daily-planet/new-light-on-the-lunar-poles-156800678/); NASA Mars in depth (https://solarsystem.nasa.gov/planets/mars/in-depth.amp); NASA Earth Observatory (https://science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-observatory/irans-lut-desert-153634)

Mars: About 58 °C in AIR (Viking 1 lander site: -89 to -31 °C over a day); ground swing not in our sources
Can Earth match it?: Yes for Mars (air figure); far short for the Moon
What it means for testing: Thermal cycling in the Lut covers Mars's daily swing, not the Moon's
Sources: Azarderakhsh et al. 2020 (https://modarch.gsfc.nasa.gov/sci_team/pubs/abstract_new.php?id=38105); NASA Mars fact sheet (https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/marsfact.html); Viking weather sensors (https://arcnav.psi.edu/urn:nasa:pds:context:instrument:met.vl2)

What it means for testing: Good match for dry-soil and life-detection tests

Mars: Dust devils and storms (dust devils seen at Arcadia Planitia)
Earth's closest: Dust lifted on about 65% of days
Can Earth match it?: As a process, yes; Earth air is far denser
What it means for testing: Good for dust mitigation and forecasting ideas, not exact physics
Sources: ESA Mars Express (https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Space_Science/Mars_Express/Earth_tones_on_Mars); Washington et al. 2009 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2791565)

Moon: No atmosphere or global magnetic field
Mars: Thin atmosphere, no global magnetic field
What it means for testing: UV tests partly; radiation needs labs
